source_text: ἀγένητος ζωὴ σύστασις τῆς γενητῆς ἀνθρώπων φύσεως ὑπάρχει. 15.20 Τό «καὶ τὸ φῶς ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ φαίνει καὶ ἡ σκοτία αὐτὸ οὐ κατέλαβεν» οὐκ ἀνέχεται τῶν αἱρετικῶν δοξασμάτων. οὐ κρυφίως γὰρ καὶ ἄγαν δριμέως δηλοῖ, ὡς ὅνπερ ἄν τις προχρόνιον χρόνον ἢ ἀκαιριαίαν ῥοπὴν ἢ προαιώνιον αἰῶνα ὑπολάβῃ, φαίνει ἀϊδίως ὡς ἀχώριστον ἀπαύγασμα τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ οὔποτε σκοτία ἀνυπαρξίας αὐτὸ κατέλαβεν. 15.21 Τό «ὁ παντοκράτωρ» οὐδὲ ἑρμηνείας δεῖται. δείκνυσι γὰρ ἀδιαίρετον ἔχειν πρὸς τὸν θεὸν πατέρα καὶ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ τὴν βασιλείαν καὶ εἶναι «ἐπὶ πάντων θεόν». 15.22 Τό «ὁ ἐρχόμενος» τὸν υἱὸν δηλοῖ μέλλοντα ἔρχεσθαι τὸ δεύτερον καὶ «κρίνειν ζῶντας καὶ νεκρούς». 15.23 Συνιστῶν τοίνυν καὶ ὁ βαπτιστὴς Ἰωάννης, ὅτι τό «ὁ ὤν» περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ εἴρηται, δηλοῖ τῷ δεσπότῃ· «σὺ εἶ» ἀντὶ τοῦ ἐκεῖνος ὁ ὤν, ὃν καὶ ἐν τῇ μήτρᾳ σε ὄντα τῆς παρθένου θεὸν ἐπιγνοὺς αὐτὸς ἐγὼ ἐν τῇ νηδύϊ τῆς στείρας ὢν διὰ τῆς σκιρτήσεως προσεκύνησα «ἢ ἕτερον προσδοκῶμεν;» 15.24 Καὶ ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ δὲ ἐπιστολῇ Ἰωάννης ὁ φίλος καὶ ἀπόστολος τοῦ κυρίου γράφει· «ὃ ἦν ἀπ' ἀρχῆς, ὃ ἀκηκόαμεν, ὃ ἑωράκαμεν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς ἡμῶν, ὃ ἐθεασάμεθα καὶ αἱ χεῖρες ἡμῶν ἐψηλάφησαν, περὶ τοῦ λόγου τῆς ζωῆς–καὶ ἡ ζωὴ ἐφανερώθη, καὶ ἑωράκαμεν καὶ μαρτυροῦμεν καὶ ἀπαγγέλλομεν ὑμῖν τὴν ζωὴν τὴν αἰώνιον, ἥτις ἦν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα καὶ ἐφανερώθη ἡμῖν–ὃ ἑωράκαμεν καὶ ἀκηκόαμεν, ἀπαγγέλλομεν καὶ ὑμῖν, ἵνα καὶ ὑμεῖς κοινωνίαν ἔχητε μεθ' ἡμῶν. καὶ ἡ κοινωνία δὲ ἡ ἡμετέρα μετὰ τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ μετὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ». 15.25 Πρόσχες καὶ αὖθις τῷ πλήθει τοῦ «ἦν», καὶ ὡς κοινωνίαν σωτηρίας οὐκ ἔχουσιν μετὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ἢ τοῦ μονογενοῦς οἱ μὴ ὁμολογοῦντες κατὰ φύσιν υἱὸν εἶναι αὐτὸν συνάναρχον τοῦ θεοῦ. 15.26 πρὸς ταύτην γὰρ ἡμῖν τὴν πίστιν τὴν 8 παραδοθεῖσαν ἐν τῇ μυσταγωγίᾳ τοῦ φωτίσματος παρὰ τοῦ πάντων δεσπότου ἐστὶν ἡ κοινωνία ἣν Πέτρος ἔγραψεν· «ἵνα γένησθε θείας κοινωνοὶ φύσεως». τὸ γὰρ κτίσμα καὶ ὑπὸ χρόνον ὂν οὐ θεία φύσις ἐστίν. 15.27 Μέμνησο δὲ πρὸς τούτοις, ὅτιπερ «τὴν κοινωνίαν ἡμῶν» εἶπεν «μετὰ τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ», ἰσοτίμως, καὶ οὐχί «διὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ». 15.28 Καὶ ὁ Ἀμὼς δὲ προφητεύων «παντοκράτορα» ὁμοίως τὸν υἱὸν ὀνομάζει οὕτω που λέγων· «ὁ οἰκοδομῶν εἰς οὐρανὸν τὴν ἀνάβασιν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ γῆς θεμελιῶν, ὁ προσκαλούμενος τὸ ὕδωρ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ ἐκχέων αὐτὸ ἐπὶ πρόσωπον πάσης τῆς γῆς, κύριος, ὁ θεός, ὁ παντοκράτωρ ὄνομα αὐτῷ». 15.29 Περὶ ἦς ἀναβάσεως ψάλλει καὶ ∆αυΐδ· «ἀνέβη ὁ θεὸς ἐν ἀλαλαγμῷ, κύριος ἐν φωνῇ σάλπιγγος». 15.30 Ἄμφω ταῦτα περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ. ὁ γὰρ πατὴρ οὔτε κατέβη οὔτε ἀνέβη, ὡς ὁ ἀπόστολος ἑρμηνεύει γράφων ὧδε· «τὸ δὲ «ἀνέβη» τί ἐστιν, εἰ μὴ ὅτι καὶ κατέβη πρῶτον; ὁ καταβὰς αὐτός ἐστιν καὶ ὁ ἀναβὰς ὑπεράνω πάντων τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἵνα πληρώσῃ τὰ πάντα» ὡς πάντων φησὶν ὑπερανεστηκὼς καὶ ὑπερφέρων ὁμοῦ τῷ τεκόντι πατρί, ἅτε ἀγένητος. 15.31 φανερὸς γάρ ἐστι τοῦτο νοήσας, ἀφ' ὧν καὶ αἱ νοεραὶ δυνάμεις, ἐπειδὴ κτίσματα μεμετρημένα τυγχάνουσιν οὖσαι ἐν οὐρανῷ, ἀλλ' οὐχ ὑπεράνω τῶν οὐρανῶν, οὐδὲ πληροῦσαι τὰ πάντα εἰσίν. 15.32 Καὶ Σοφωνίας «παντοκράτορα» ὡσαύτως ἀναγορεύει αὐτὸν λέγων· «αὕτη αὐτοῖς ἀντὶ τῆς ὕβρεως αὐτῶν, διότι ὠνείδισαν καὶ ἐμεγαλύνθησαν ἐπὶ τὸν κύριον τὸν παντοκράτορα. ἐπιφανήσεται κύριος ἐπ' αὐτούς, καὶ ἐξολο θρεύσει κύριος πάντας τοὺς θεοὺς τῶν ἐθνῶν τῆς γῆς, καὶ προκυνήσουσιν ἕκαστος ἐκ τοῦ τόπου αὐτοῦ». 15.33 Καὶ Μαλαχίας ἑπομένως ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ δεσπότου φάσκει· «διότι ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν ἡλίου καὶ ἕως δυσμῶν δεδόξασταί μου τὸ ὄνομα ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν καὶ ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ θυμίαμα προσάγεται τῷ ὀνοματί μου καὶ θυσία καθαρά. διότι μέγα τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, λέγει κύριος παντοκράτωρ. ὑμεῖς δὲ βεβηλοῦτε αὐτό». 15.34 Ἡ γὰρ μνήμη τῆς τε ἐπιφανείας καὶ τοῦ δοξάζεσθαι ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, τὸν υἱὸν σημαίνεσθαι δείκνυσιν, οὗ τὸ ὄνομα βεβηλοῦσιν Ἰουδαῖοι σὺν τοῖς κτισματολάτραις. καὶ αὐτὴ δὲ ἡ ἀκολουθία παντοκράτορα αὐτὸν εἶναι βούλεται, καθὸ εἰκὼν καὶ μονογενὴς παντοκράτορος κεχρεωστημένος τὸ καὶ ἐν τούτῳ εἰκὼν νοεῖσθαι τοῦ παντοκράτορος. 15.35 Καὶ Παῦλος δὲ Ἑβραίοις γράφει· «ὃς ὢν ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης τοῦ πατρός», τοῦτ' ἔστιν συνάναρχος καὶ ὁμοούσιος. ἵνα γὰρ τὰ ἀπαράβλητα παραβολικῶς πως παραδειχθείη, εἰ κἂν οὕτω ποσῶς εἰς νοῦν δεχθείη τὸ ὑπὲρ νοῦν,
pass_a_gloss: [...this] unoriginate life is the constitution of the originate nature of men. 15.20 The 'and the light shines in the darkness and the darkness did not seize it' does not endure the opinions of the heretics. For not secretly and very sharply it shows that whatever time before time or momentary instant or age before the ages someone may suppose, he shines eternally as inseparable radiance of God, and never did darkness of non-existence seize it. 15.21 The 'the Almighty' does not even need interpretation. For it shows him to have the kingdom undivided with God the Father and his Holy Spirit, and to be 'God over all'. 15.22 The 'the one coming' shows the Son who is about to come the second time and 'to judge living and dead'. 15.23 So, establishing also, John the Baptist, that the 'the one being' has been said about the Son, shows it to the Master: 'you are', in place of: that one being, whom also, you being God in the womb of the virgin, having recognized, I myself being in the belly of the barren one worshipped through the leaping, 'or are we to expect another?' 15.24 And in the first letter John the friend and apostle of the Lord writes: 'what was from beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we gazed on and our hands felt, about the Word of the life, and the life was made manifest, and we have seen and bear witness and report to you the eternal life, which was toward the Father and was made manifest to us, what we have seen and heard we report also to you, so that you too may have fellowship with us. And our fellowship is with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ'. 15.25 Attend again to the multitude of the 'was', and how those not confessing him to be Son by nature, without beginning together with God, do not have fellowship of salvation with the Father or the only-begotten. 15.26 For in relation to this faith handed down to us in the initiation teaching of the illumination by the Master of all is the fellowship that Peter wrote: 'so that you may become sharers of divine nature'. For the thing made and being under time is not divine nature. 15.27 And remember besides these, that he said 'our fellowship' 'with the Father and his Son', in equal honour, and not 'through his Son'. 15.28 And Amos too, prophesying, likewise names the Son 'Almighty', saying somewhere thus: 'the one building into heaven his ascent and founding his promise upon earth, the one calling forth the water of the sea and pouring it out upon the face of all the earth, Lord, the God, the Almighty is name to him'. 15.29 About which ascent David also sings: 'God went up in shouting, Lord in sound of trumpet'. 15.30 Both these are about the Son. For the Father neither went down nor went up, as the apostle interprets, writing thus: 'and the [word] went up, what is it, if not that he also went down first? The one who went down is himself also the one who went up above all the heavens, so that he may fill all things', as, he says, having risen above all and surpassing, together with the Father who bore him, as being unoriginate. 15.31 For he is evident having understood this, from the fact that the intellectual powers too, since they happen to be measured creatures, are in heaven, but not above the heavens, nor are they filling all things. 15.32 And Zephaniah likewise proclaims him 'Almighty', saying: 'this [is] to them in place of their insolence, because they reproached and were magnified against the Lord the Almighty. The Lord will appear against them, and the Lord will utterly destroy all the gods of the nations of the earth, and they will worship, each from his place'. 15.33 And Malachi, following on, says from the person of the Master: 'because from risings of the sun and to settings my name has been glorified among the nations, and in every place incense is brought to my name and a clean sacrifice. Because great is my name among the nations, says Lord Almighty. But you profane it'. 15.34 For the mention both of the appearing and of being glorified among the nations shows the Son to be signified, whose name Jews profane with the worshippers of a creature. And the sequence itself wants him to be Almighty, in so far as, being image and only-begotten of the Almighty, he is owed to be understood as image of the Almighty in this too. 15.35 And Paul writes to Hebrews: 'who being radiance of the glory of the Father', that is, without beginning together and of one essence. For so that the incomparable things be shown somehow by comparison, if even thus in some measure the thing above mind be received into mind, [...]
pass_b_english: … unoriginate life is what holds together the originate nature of human beings.

“And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not grasp it” (John 1:5) does not tolerate the opinions of the heretics. For it shows, not obscurely but with great sharpness, that whatever time before time, or briefest instant, or age before the ages anyone may suppose, he shines eternally as the inseparable radiance of God, and the darkness of non-existence never grasped it.

“The Almighty” (Revelation 1:8) needs no interpretation at all. For it shows that he holds the kingdom undivided with God the Father and his Holy Spirit, and that he is “God over all” (Romans 9:5). “Who is to come” (Revelation 1:8) shows the Son, who is going to come a second time and “judge the living and the dead” (2 Timothy 4:1).

So John the Baptist too, establishing that “He who is” was said of the Son, makes it plain when he says to the Master, “Are you” (that is, are you that One who is, whom, when you were God in the womb of the Virgin, I myself, being in the belly of the barren woman, recognized and worshipped by my leaping), “or do we look for another?” (Matthew 11:3).

And John, the friend and apostle of the Lord, writes in his first epistle as well: “That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon and our hands have handled, concerning the Word of life (and the life was made manifest, and we have seen it, and bear witness, and declare to you the eternal life, which was with the Father and was made manifest to us), that which we have seen and heard we declare to you also, so that you too may have fellowship with us. And our fellowship is with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ” (1 John 1:1-3).

Mark once more how often he says “was,” and how those who do not confess that he is Son by nature, without beginning together with God, have no fellowship of salvation with the Father or with the Only-begotten. For it is in this faith, handed down to us by the Master of all in the mystery-teaching of the illumination, that we have the fellowship of which Peter wrote, “that you may become partakers of the divine nature” (2 Peter 1:4). For a creature, a thing subject to time, is not divine nature.
Remember besides that he said “our fellowship” is “with the Father and with his Son,” with equal honour, and not “through his Son.”

And Amos too, in his prophecy, likewise names the Son “Almighty,” saying somewhere like this: “He who builds his ascent into heaven, and lays the foundation of his promise upon the earth; who calls the water of the sea and pours it out upon the face of all the earth: the Lord God Almighty is his name” (Amos 9:6). Of this ascent David too sings: “God went up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet” (Psalm 47:5).

Both these sayings are about the Son. For the Father neither came down nor went up, as the Apostle explains when he writes: “Now what does ‘he went up’ mean, if not that he also first came down? He who came down is the very one who also went up far above all the heavens, that he might fill all things” (Ephesians 4:9-10). He means: as one who has risen above all things and surpasses them, together with the Father who begot him, since he is unoriginate. For it is plain that he understood it so, from the fact that the spiritual powers, too, since they are measured creatures, are in heaven, but not above the heavens, and do not fill all things.

And Zephaniah likewise proclaims him “Almighty,” saying: “This shall be theirs in return for their insolence, because they reproached and magnified themselves against the Lord Almighty. The Lord will appear against them, and the Lord will utterly destroy all the gods of the nations of the earth, and they will worship him, each from his own place” (Zephaniah 2:10-11).

And Malachi, following on, says in the person of the Master: “For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name has been glorified among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure sacrifice; for my name is great among the nations, says the Lord Almighty. But you profane it” (Malachi 1:11-12).

For the mention both of his appearing and of his being glorified among the nations shows that the Son is meant, whose name the Jews profane together with those who worship a creature. And the very sequence of the text requires him to be Almighty, since, as image and only-begotten of the Almighty, he must be understood as image of the Almighty in this too.

And Paul writes to the Hebrews: “who, being the radiance of the glory of the Father” (Hebrews 1:3), that is, without beginning together with him and of one essence with him. For so that things beyond comparison might be shown somehow by a comparison, if even so what is beyond the mind might be taken into the mind in some measure, …

choices.issue: Old draft garbled, split and mis-referenced
choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. The old English printed edition numbers 15.20-15.28 in the reading text; split 15.28 into 'And Amos' and 'And the prophet'; gave the Zephaniah quotation (15.32) to 'Wisdom'; turned οὐ κρυφίως (not obscurely) into 'secretly', συνάναρχον (without beginning together) into 'co-ruling', ὑπερφέρων (surpassing) into 'carrying [all things] above', and made ἅτε ἀγένητος a title of the Father instead of the Son; garbled 15.23 ('in the desert of the wilderness and through the fluttering') and 15.34 ('having been endowed with Pantokrator'); misread 15.31. References: 2 Thess 2:8 for 'who is to come' replaced by Revelation 1:8; Acts 10:42 for 'judge the living and the dead' replaced by 2 Timothy 4:1 (wording); Exodus 3:14 dropped (not quoted here); Zephaniah 2:10-11, Amos 9:6, Ephesians 4:9-10 and Matthew 11:3 added; Malachi 1:11 widened to 1:11-12; abbreviations written in full.

choices.english: … unoriginate life is what holds together
choices.why: The section opens mid-sentence (15.19 'For he says: this'); only the words this section holds are translated, with a leading ellipsis.
Standard English for the Septuagint title; the old draft left it as 'Pantokrator'.

choices.term: «σὺ εἶ» ἀντὶ τοῦ ἐκεῖνος ὁ ὤν
choices.english: “Are you” (that is, are you that One who is, …)
choices.why: Didymus reads the Baptist's 'You are' in Matthew 11:3 as naming 'He who is'. His explanation is set in parentheses inside the quotation, which resumes with 'or do we look for another?'.

choices.english: in the mystery-teaching of the illumination
choices.why: φώτισμα is the common patristic name for baptism; kept as Didymus says it, without adding the word 'baptism'.

choices.term: ὡς πάντων … ὑπερανεστηκὼς καὶ ὑπερφέρων … ἅτε ἀγένητος
choices.english: as one who has risen above all things and surpasses them … since he is unoriginate
choices.why: The participles and ἅτε ἀγένητος describe the Son who went up; the old draft gave 'unbegotten' to the Father.

choices.term: φανερὸς γάρ ἐστι τοῦτο νοήσας, ἀφ' ὧν
choices.english: For it is plain that he understood it so, from the fact that
choices.why: Personal construction ('he is evident as having understood'); English makes it impersonal. The proof is that the angelic powers are in heaven, not above it.

choices.english: they will worship, will utterly destroy
choices.why: προκυνήσουσιν is a misprint for προσκυνήσουσιν; ἐξολο θρεύσει is split by a line break. 'Him' after 'worship' is English idiom for the bare verb.
The '8' is a printed line number in the copy-text (page debris); skipped.
Didymus' polemical word for those who worship the Son while calling him a creature; kept as a description.

choices.term: κεχρεωστημένος τὸ καὶ ἐν τούτῳ εἰκὼν νοεῖσθαι
choices.english: he must be understood as image of the Almighty in this too
choices.why: Perfect passive of χρεωστέω, 'being owed / bound': the image must match its original in being almighty.

choices.english: without beginning together with him and of one essence with him
choices.why: Didymus' gloss on 'radiance'; both terms rendered in plain words.

choices.term: εἰς νοῦν δεχθείη τὸ ὑπὲρ νοῦν,
choices.english: what is beyond the mind might be taken into the mind in some measure, …
